selected.first_distribution_hypothesis: Approach one small Chilean seller with a documented returns problem and request a no-purchase pilot of 10–30 units from a single category. Record condition, handling cost, time to relist, sale price, refunds, and unsold inventory. Use the seller’s existing marketplace account or a pre-approved outlet rather than assuming permission to resell. Falsify at the lowest cost by asking five sellers for anonymized counts of returned units and whether they would release a small batch on consignment; stop if no seller provides inventory, resale permissions, or a verifiable disposition price.
selected.next_no_spend_buyer_test: Select one specific product/problem. Verify alternatives, landed or fulfilment costs, return/refund exposure, and whether a real buyer would pay; no store launch or supplier order is authorised.
selected.title: Narrow Chilean e-commerce returns-recovery test for one product category

selected.first_distribution_hypothesis: Start without seeking production access or regulatory permissions: download the CMF NCG 514 materials and developer-portal specifications, build a small validator for one publicly specified data-exchange flow, and test it against self-created fixtures. Then contact Chilean fintechs, banks, cooperatives, card issuers, or implementation vendors only to ask whether they already possess an internal conformance harness and which test artifacts they must produce. Falsification threshold: stop if at least 10 relevant organizations or vendors show no need for external validation, already have equivalent tooling, or cannot identify a budget owner. The verifiable participation catalyst is the CMF's July 2027 implementation target and the publication of technical specifications; no buyer, sale, margin, or permission is assumed.
selected.next_no_spend_buyer_test: Identify one genuinely budget-owning regulated buyer, one conformance failure, and an independently accepted paid software deliverable before coding a broad financial integration.
selected.title: Chile SFA conformance-testing wedge ahead of the July 2027 implementation date

selected.first_distribution_hypothesis: Use the SEC's public installer and technical-documentation pages to identify 10 authorized distributed-generation installers. Send a one-page sample checklist covering RGR N°06/2024, AFCI status, equipment authorization and required filing fields. Ask whether they would pay for one review of a real but anonymized project, without promising approval. Test with one paid or explicitly unpaid pilot only after the installer confirms the scope. Falsify if installers report that they already perform the review internally, will not share a redacted equipment list, or do not value error reduction enough to accept a trial. Do not install, certify or submit electrical work without the required authorization.
selected.next_no_spend_buyer_test: Obtain a buyer's actual equipment/inspection requirement, a real supplier cost and applicable Chilean regulatory conditions first.
selected.title: BESS and inverter compliance pre-check for Chilean distributed-energy projects

selected.first_distribution_hypothesis: Identify one existing Chilean hydroponic or controlled-environment grower willing to share two comparable production cycles. Measure lighting, HVAC and pump electricity; record kilograms harvested and sale prices; run one controlled lighting-schedule change while keeping crop and harvest criteria constant. Stop if the grower cannot provide baseline meter data, comparable harvest records or permission to alter the schedule. Do not invest in a new farm based on the cited evidence alone.
selected.next_no_spend_buyer_test: Find a real operator's measured baseline and proposed savings, plus equipment/installation prices, before a product or pilot.
selected.title: Indoor-farm lighting and energy audit wedge for existing Chilean growers
